A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper, with readable main text, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–2, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: v2 presents theoretical characterizations and proofs. Its Limitations section explicitly defers empirical comparisons to future work; the appendices contain no original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 retains the purely theoretical investigation and the statement deferring empirical comparisons to future work. No original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes appear in its appendices.

M1.justification: The UHAT architecture assumptions, attention rules, and B-RASP/LTL/automaton constructions are unchanged. Definition D.3 clarifies hardmax's existing role as the normalization function without altering the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The formal-language examples and theoretical coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baselines. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons among transformer classes and equivalent formalisms.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing protocols, and none are introduced in v3.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. The illustrative attention constructions are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. Table 1's expressivity relationships and the theoretical findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, bounds, constructions, and proofs retain their mathematical content. Definition D.3 replaces a redundant identity with an explicit reference to the existing hardmax normalization; layer-index edits and subsequent equation renumbering are not substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same leftmost/rightmost expressivity separation, characterize leftmost UHATs through the past-only LTL fragment and POFAs, and establish the same connection to finite-precision soft attention.

C2.justification: Sections 3.3 and 8 retain the interpretations involving flip-flop languages, recency biases, and expressivity hierarchies. The applicability assumptions and limitations concerning learnability, training, and future empirical investigation are unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware information, training times, or code/data-access information are added or removed. Appendix D's edits clarify the existing formalization.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Removing the duplicated surname 'Brzozowski' from the Cohen and Brzozowski (1971) reference is a bibliographic correction, not a citation addition or removal.

P1.justification: v3 replaces 'App.' references with section symbols, corrects the duplicated surname, changes layer indices to parenthesized superscripts in Eqs. (31)–(32), and clarifies Definition D.3. The narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 1–2 retain their content and design. The redundant displayed equation in Definition D.3 becomes inline text, accompanied by small spacing and pagination changes, including the start of Section B.5 moving onto page 10.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves technical clarity. Definition D.3 replaces v2's tautological hardmax equation with an explicit connection to normalization in Eq. (30c), while Eqs. (31)–(32) distinguish layer indices from position projections. These limited repairs make the formalization easier to follow; the scientific contribution and supporting proofs remain stable.
